newsitem.title: USA: Comcast, ABC to buy major E! stake.
newsitem.headline: Comcast, ABC to buy major E! stake.

text.p: Comcast Corp and Walt Disney Co's ABC Cable Networks Tuesday said they agreed to form a new organization to acquire a majority interest in E! Entertainment Television for undisclosed terms.

Brian Roberts, president of Comcast, and Michael Eisner, chairman and chief executive of Disney, said the new organization plans to hold a 68.8 percent ownership of E! Entertainment Television. E! is a cable service that provides more than 42 million subscribers with entertainment programming as well as news and information about the entertainment world and its personalities.

Comcast obtained the right to increase its ownership of E! Entertainment to 68.8 percent based on a recently triggered buy/sell agreement between the owners. Comcast already owns 10.4 percent and the remainder will be acquired from Time Warner Inc.
The acquisition of the shares from Time Warner is subject to compliance with the filing and waiting period requirements under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Act.
The agreement has been approved by the boards of directors of both companies.
E! Entertainment Television will be managed by Comcast's programming partnership C3 (Comcast Content & Communications).
ABC's ownership in cable properties includes ESPN, ESPN2, ESPNews, Disney Channel, Lifetime, A&E and History Channel.
Disney and Comcast executives said E! Entertainment Television will continue with its current programming concept.

E! Entertainment Television was formed in 1987. With the new venture's acquisition of Time Warner's share of E! Entertainment Television, remaining minority partners will be subsidiaries of Cox Communications Inc, Continental Cablevision and Liberty Media Corp, each with 10.4 percent interests.
